title: Objectwise module sections and their unbounded derived functor
statement: Work in the universes and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $U$ an object of $\mathcal C$. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define $\Gamma(U,-):\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Ab}$ by sending a module sheaf $M$ to its abelian group $M(U)$, forgetting its $\mathcal O(U)$-action, and a module-sheaf morphism to its component at $U$. On the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], define $R\Gamma(U,-):D(\mathcal A)\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ to be the total right derived functor of $\Gamma(U,-)$. Concretely, choose a K-injective representative [def-pur-kinjective-complex], whose existence is supplied by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], apply $\Gamma(U,-)$ termwise and localize the resulting abelian-group complex; morphisms are induced by the right-derived construction. The functor includes its standard natural comparison from termwise sections into its total right derived functor; on a K-injective complex this comparison is an isomorphism. All coefficient, module and section groups lie in a universe bounding both site universes; the localization universes are chosen as in the size convention.

source.place: Section Cohomology of unbounded complexes (section-unbounded), example (2), defining Γ(U,-) and RΓ(U,-); Tag 0D6K (lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim), and Tag 0BKY.
